problem: The horizontal asymptote of the function $f(x)=\frac{{x}^{2}-8{x}^{3}}{2{x}^{3}-5x}$ is $y=${{field-1}}.

feedback.problem: The horizontal asymptote of the function $f(x)=\frac{8{x}^{4}+6x}{({x}^{2}-2x)(1-2{x}^{2})}$ is $y=${{field-1}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
The given function can be rewritten as follows:

$$
f(x)=\frac{8{x}^{4}-6x}{-2{x}^{4}+4{x}^{3}+{x}^{2}-2x}
$$

To find the horizontal asymptote of a rational function, we divide every term in the numerator and denominator by the dominant term in the denominator, and then we let $x\to \infty .$

Ignoring the coefficient, the dominant term in the denominator is ${x}^{4}.$ So, we divide every term in the numerator and denominator by ${x}^{4},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{8{x}^{4}-6x}{-2{x}^{4}+4{x}^{3}+{x}^{2}-2x} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{8{x}^{4}}{{x}^{4}}-\frac{6x}{{x}^{4}})}{(-\frac{2{x}^{4}}{{x}^{4}}+\frac{4{x}^{3}}{{x}^{4}}+\frac{{x}^{2}}{{x}^{4}}-\frac{2x}{{x}^{4}})} \\  & =\frac{(8-\frac{6}{{x}^{3}})}{(-2+\frac{4}{x}+\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{2}{{x}^{3}})}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, when $x$ is very large, the terms $\frac{6}{{x}^{3}},$ $\frac{4}{x},$ $\frac{1}{{x}^{2}},$ and $\frac{2}{{x}^{3}}$ become very small. Therefore, as $x\to \infty ,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{(8-\frac{6}{{x}^{3}})}{(-2+\frac{4}{x}+\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}-\frac{2}{{x}^{3}})} \\  & \to \frac{8-0}{-2+0+0-0} \\  & =-4.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the horizontal asymptote is $y=-4.$
